scope: Proposed implementation prerequisites inferred from observed product relationships, not the reference implementation. No framework/database/service topology chosen.

nodes.name: Resolve architecture and document gaps
nodes.reason: Owner decisions and ADRs before technology choices or scaffolding.

nodes.name: Identity, access and venue context
nodes.reason: Secure account/venue boundary and permission contract.

nodes.name: Data contracts and persistence foundations
nodes.reason: Define independent schema and migration/test approach; no reference backend inference.

nodes.name: Navigation shell and verification harness
nodes.reason: Route shell, accessibility, test and contract gates; separate from data-driven Home dashboard.

nodes.name: Home
nodes.reason: Home summaries consume reservation and request read models; navigation shell is separate foundation work.

nodes.name: Reservations
nodes.reason: Reservation lifecycle and table assignment precede dependent widget, sales and reporting journeys.

nodes.name: Requests
nodes.reason: Request intake uses client and availability context; conversion to reservation is optional pending safe validation.

nodes.name: Clients
nodes.reason: Client identity and profile linkage precede a unified reservation or request journey.

nodes.name: Marketing
nodes.reason: Marketing uses client, reservation and guest-facing communication context.

nodes.name: Voice AI
nodes.reason: Voice-assisted booking needs reservation and availability contracts; external service remains optional.

nodes.name: Online Sales
nodes.reason: Offers and upgrades attach to reservation/client context; payment integration remains separately gated.

nodes.name: Reporting
nodes.reason: Core reports consume verified transactional records; detailed parity remains deferred.

nodes.name: General Settings
nodes.reason: Venue context and configuration are needed for venue-scoped records.

nodes.name: Integrations
nodes.reason: External connectors are separately gated and must not determine core reservation correctness.

nodes.name: Availability
nodes.reason: Shifts, access rules, party-size/time availability and pacing precede booking eligibility.

nodes.name: Widgets
nodes.reason: Booking widget consumes availability, reservation handling and guest-facing language.

nodes.name: Floorplan
nodes.reason: Rooms, tables, seating areas and layout selection are inputs to shift seating and assignment.

nodes.name: People
nodes.reason: Identity and current-account access gates precede restricted settings and guest data.

nodes.name: Guest-Facing Language
nodes.reason: Guest-facing policies and language are displayed in dependent communication and widget journeys.

nodes.name: Imports
nodes.reason: Imports target client and reservation concepts with safe reconciliation.

notes: Hard edges determine prerequisites; optional integrations are separately gated and do not enter the DAG.
SCR-140/141 are mapped to Clients despite registry domain DOM-02 because the guest link opens the client profile; the original classification is retained as registryDomainId.
External payment execution, scheduling and messages require isolated test fixtures; no production write is used to validate mapping.
